name: Wurm
prior: Benjolin (Rob Hordijk 2009): two oscillators, state-variable filter and the rungler, 'an 8-step shift register that takes its data input from one oscillator (OSC A) and its clock input from the other (OSC B)', 3-bit DAC -> 'stepped voltage pattern of variable length and depth' fed back to both oscillators (VS: veryfriendlymusic.com 'How to play a Benjolin in 2026'; community.vcvrack.com Benjolin patch thread; R: synthesis.md 2.6). Hardware: After Later Audio Benjolin V2 (Eurorack, USD 325, 8/16 and 127-step modes, external clock, supports Music Thing Turing Machine expanders; VS: afterlateraudio.com/products/benjolin-v2), Epoch Modular Benjolin (VS: modulargrid.net/e/epoch-modular-benjolin). Software: VCV Rack 'Benjolin V2 emulator' and 'Planet Rungler' patches (VS: patchstorage.com), gen~ rungler patch '[sharing is rungling] stepped havoc in gen~' (VS: cycling74.com forums), SuperCollider patch (VS: scsynth.org/t/6599); no iOS app, no VST/AU/M4L device found (VS: three searches; a 'there is one in miRack' forum remark is unverified). The scale-locked half of the idea is a Eurorack idiom: Music Thing Modular Turing Machine = shift-register 'clocked stepped randomly changing control voltages that can be locked into loops of repeating notes', with a quantizer 'riffs that sound musical' (VS: synthtopia.com/?p=137786; perfectcircuit.com 2hp Turing Machine); EMW T-Sequencer = Turing Machine + quantizer (VS: synthtopia 2023/07/06); Flatsix 'Shroud of Turing' 16-bit shift register with musical quantization (VS: reverb.com); 'Turing Machine for Ableton Live' (VS: isotonikstudios.com). Not found: the register under a finger with the havoc depth as Hoehe, in the key, persisting per Puls lane between hits.
costNotes: L1 native: OSC 0.06 + biquad 0.06 + WaveShaper (oversample none) 0.06 + 2-3 gains 0.09 = ~0.3, plus the detune-bus gain; the JS rungler runs in tick() every 25 ms (Worker clock, APP 6043) and costs nothing audible; 0.4 is a safe figure. All frequency/filter changes must be scheduled ahead of the 0.12-0.35 s horizon (APP 6039), which is exactly what 'Flanken vorausberechnet' says; at takt 40 Hz that is 5-14 edges per tick. L3 worklet (two triangles, register, DAC, SVF at audio rate): the measured 2-table-oscillator + tanh + 1-pole core is 0.24 units (R: webaudio.md section 4), + SVF ~0.1, + node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09 = ~0.5-0.65 for one worm; the second 7-bit worm on the right adds ~0.3 -> ~0.9 if both run in one node.
soundHeld: Simulated (M: ideas/check/sim/perf_wrm_sim.js, 2000 clocks, kopplung 0.5, y=1, spanne 4, 2 % bit flips). With feedback only into the clock oscillator (as specified: f_B') the register falls into rigid loops: fA/fB = 0.618 gives a cycle of exactly 8 clocks (a Turing-Machine loop), 1.37/6 -> 29 clocks, 2.71 -> 24 clocks with only 4 distinct DAC values; with the Benjolin topology (r modulates both oscillators) the cycles stretch to 34-69 clocks with 6-8 distinct values and changes on 98-99 % of clocks - 'nie zufaellig, nie identisch' needs the data oscillator in the loop too. Near-synchronous rates (fA = 1.017 fB) stall: DAC stuck at 7 for 28 clocks and the register all-ones for 23 clocks despite the 2 % flips (one deg value 83 % of the time) - keep fA/fB away from simple ratios (golden ratio times the kopplung term) and reset on a stall. The degree map round((r-0.5)*2*spanne*y) with r=(R&7)/7 yields {-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4} at y=1 - the root never sounds at full depth; use a 3-bit -> degree table that contains 0. y works as advertised: y=0 one degree, 0.25 three, 0.5 five, 1 eight (histogram in the sim). kopplung 0-1 changed the cycle length (38 -> 69) but not the step density. The base tone at y=0 (triangle -> resonant LP -> tanh) is an ordinary mono-synth voice; the identity of the engine is entirely in the register's behaviour, which is fine for the performer brief but gives the sound designer nothing new in the timbre at level 1 - the audio-rate L3 rungler (f_B > 50 Hz) is where the Benjolin 'havoc' lives.
soundBurst: Burst steps n = max(1, floor(gate*f_B)): at the default takt 6 Hz every gate up to 0.33 s advances ONE step (M), so a Puls hit plays a single pitch from the register - a Turing-Machine melody lane in key (musical, persistent per lane, 'jeder Schlag ein neues Fragment' is really 'jeder Schlag die naechste Note'); the 'stuttering inside a hit' only happens at takt >= 12-20 Hz (3 steps per 160 ms gate at 20 Hz, 6 at 40 Hz). Since hit() for sustain engines uses burst:true with gate 0.22 s (APP 5083) and lanes give 0.9*step (APP 5980), the lane experience at 84-120 bpm is one note per hit unless takt is raised; burstEnv frames it cleanly. Two fingers on the same bus share one register (A.wrmReg[bus]), so 'zwei Finger = zwei Wuermer' needs per-voice registers for fingers and per-lane registers for the Puls. Takt in Hz without a running Puls lets two fingers drift apart; grid it to a master clock (the app's tempo) always, not only when SEQ.on.
failureModes: Feedback only into the clock oscillator gives rigid 8-29-clock loops (M); the Benjolin feeds the rungler into both oscillators - do that or it is a plain Turing Machine
Near-synchronous A/B rates stall the register (DAC stuck 28 clocks, all-ones 23 clocks despite 2 % flips, M): keep the ratio irrational-ish and reset on stalls
Degree map has no 0 at full depth: the root never sounds; use a 3-bit -> degree table including 0
At the default takt (6 Hz) a Puls hit is one note, not a 1-4-step stutter; the stutter needs takt >= 12-20 Hz
Level-1 timbre is an ordinary triangle/LP/tanh voice; the novelty is behavioural - the audio-rate L3 rungler is the sonic payoff and should not be L3-only on capable phones
Register per bus makes two fingers play the same figure; per-voice registers for fingers, per-lane for Puls
Free-running takt without Puls lets fingers drift; always grid to the master tempo
verdict: Rare: the Benjolin/rungler exists in Eurorack (After Later Benjolin V2, Epoch), as VCV/gen~/SuperCollider patches and nowhere as a touch app, while 'shift register plus quantizer = melodies in key' is the Turing-Machine idiom (Music Thing, EMW T-Sequencer, Shroud of Turing, an Ableton device); unfound is only the combination under a finger with havoc depth as Hoehe and a register that lives per Puls lane. Native plus JS tick at ~0.4 units is comfortable (L3 worklet ~0.65-0.9) and the 25 ms Worker clock with the 0.12-0.35 s horizon fits the pre-scheduled edges. The simulation shows the spec's topology fails its own promise: with feedback only into the clock the register loops rigidly every 8-29 clocks, near-synchronous rates stall it for 20-30 clocks despite the bit flips, and the degree map omits the root - feed the rungler into both oscillators (Benjolin), keep the rate ratio irrational and add 0 to the table. As a Puls lane it is a scale-locked Turing-Machine melody generator (one note per hit at the default takt, stutters only above ~12 Hz), which is musical and distinct from Schwarm's smooth chaos; the held tone itself is ordinary, so the engine's worth is its behaviour.
